overview.headline: Balanced and unbalanced forces explain level flight and aircraft motion changes

keyPoints.point: Simplified motion means we look at only one force and one direction at a time while other forces stay balanced
keyPoints.quote: we are looking at only one force and one direction at a time

keyPoints.point: Level flight at constant speed occurs when weight is balanced by lift and drag is balanced by thrust
keyPoints.quote: the weight would be balanced by the lift and the drag would be balanced by the thrust

keyPoints.point: Unbalanced forces make the aircraft move in the direction of the greater force
keyPoints.quote: If the forces become unbalanced, the aircraft will move in the direction of the greater force.

keyPoints.point: Net force is the difference between opposing forces such as lift minus weight or thrust minus drag
keyPoints.quote: The net force is the difference between the opposing forces; lift minus weight, or thrust minus drag.

keyTerms.gloss: downward force that is balanced by lift to keep aircraft level
keyTerms.quote: the weight would be balanced by the lift

keyTerms.gloss: upward force that can be balanced against weight to sustain flight
keyTerms.quote: the weight would be balanced by the lift and the drag would be balanced by the thrust

keyTerms.gloss: resistive force balanced by thrust during steady motion
keyTerms.quote: the drag would be balanced by the thrust

keyTerms.gloss: forward force that when balanced with drag keeps speed constant
keyTerms.quote: increasing the thrust while the drag is constant will cause the plane to accelerate

keyTerms.gloss: change in motion computed from net force divided by mass
keyTerms.quote: We can compute the acceleration which the aircraft will experience from Newton’s second law of motion
